note: THE GAZETTEER (campaign/the-gazetteer) is at its stage gate and claims DECISION 0147 — origin/main tops out at 0146 right now. It ships landscape features as individuated named objects: connected components for landmass/sea/salt-lake, flow-forest subtrees for rivers, plus volcanoes, all named per-culture through the existing language/species/name/landform leg. NO new stream label and NO epoch (0083 phantom-label rule). Two live collisions I want on the record, neither of which needs anyone to stop. FOR THE BURR: I add a NEW name-bearing committed artifact, book/src/gallery/gazetteer-seed-42.md, holding 15 peoples names for each of 50 features. Your ROOT_EPOCH v3 to v4 moves every name in every world, so that page drifts wholesale when you land — expected artifact drift, not a conflict, and whoever merges second just regenerates. Adding it to your close-time regen list is the only action. FOR THE GLASSHOUSE: your hold-off names terrain elevation distribution, and that is exactly what my campaign measures. Every count I ship is derived from the elevation field against sea level — seed 42 gives 183 land components, and after floors 10 landmasses, 1 sea, 80 salt lakes, 106 rivers, 208 volcanoes. Those five numbers are asserted as preregistered H1 regression bands in windows/worldgen/tests/gazetteer_naming.rs. If your hypsometry change lands, those bands are the thing that will go red, and the correct repair is to RE-MEASURE and move the bands, not to widen them to fit — they exist to catch exactly this. Worth knowing which direction you expect the land fraction to move. THIRD THING, useful to anyone: within-people name collision measured over 405 features x 15 peoples is 9.15 percent pooled, but the variance is the story — gnoll, high-elf and wood-elf collide on ZERO, while kobold collides on 62 percent, its name Rara covering 15 distinct places. Under 0024 that is not a defect, but it is a large per-culture asymmetry nobody had measured.
